v.rationale: The three are nearly identical in their core: the same migration, Fillable attribute update, FormRequest rules (present|nullable|string|max:30) and validated-only update. All suites pass, and all three passed probes for whitespace becoming null, multibyte/emoji length limits, integer rejection, form-encoded PATCH, a real token with a trailing slash, and no email in the response. The deciding probe was a guest request without an Accept: application/json header. In impl-1 and impl-2 the default guest redirect calls route('login'), which doesn't exist, so the request returns 500 instead of 401. impl-3 changed redirectGuestsTo for api/* and tests both the JSON and plain cases, so it ranks first; it is also the simplest (only() instead of a resource class). impl-1 beats impl-2 because it returns id, name and nickname at the top level as the spec describes, while impl-2 nests them under 'data', and its tests add real-token and multibyte cases. impl-2's tests are tidier (datasets, message checks), but that doesn't outweigh the response-shape difference.
